captions.linkedin:
Stop buying cheap stocks blind. Half of high book-to-market names are not undervalued. They're distressed, and distressed firms keep falling.

Joseph Piotroski (Journal of Accounting Research, 2000) built a 9-point checklist to separate the phoenixes from the zombies inside the value universe. Each signal is binary, mechanical, and pulled straight from the financial statements:

🔹 PROFITABILITY, ROA and cash flow positive and improving
🔹 LEVERAGE DROPS, deleveraging and liquidity improving
🔹 NO ISSUANCE, firms not issuing new equity shares
🔹 MARGIN IMPROVING, gross margin and asset turnover gains
🔹 ANNUAL CADENCE, 5 months post fiscal year-end data
🔹 QUALITY FOCUS, 9 binary accounting strength signals

The edge concentrates in small, illiquid, low-analyst names where information diffuses slowly. Large-cap magnitude compressed after publication as institutions adopted it.

Piotroski (2000) Journal of Accounting Research; educational only, not investment advice.
